======================================================================
ARTICLE: Multiplayer online battle arena
WIKIPEDIA REVISION TEXT
======================================================================

{{Short description|Video game genre}}
{{Redirect|MOBA||Moba (disambiguation){{!}}Moba}}
{{VG Strategy}}
'''Multiplayer online battle arena''' ('''MOBA'''){{efn|name=aka|Also known as '''action real-time strategy''' ('''ARTS''') or, more recently, as '''hero brawler''' and '''team brawler'''}} is a [[Video game genre|subgenre]] of [[strategy video game]]s in which two teams of [[Gamer|players]] compete on a structured battlefield, each controlling a single [[Player character|character]] with distinctive abilities that grow stronger as the match progresses.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Cannizzo|first1=Alejandro|last2=Ramírez|first2=Esmitt|title=Towards Procedural Map and Character Generation for the MOBA Game Genre|journal=Ingeniería y Ciencia|year=2015|volume=11|issue=22|pages=95–119|doi=10.17230/ingciencia.11.22.5|issn=1794-9165|doi-access=free|hdl=10784/7884|hdl-access=free}}</ref> The objective is to destroy the enemy team's main structure while defending one's own. In some MOBA games, the objective can be defeating every player on the enemy team. Matches emphasize team coordination, tactical choices, and real-time combat. Players are assisted by [[Artificial intelligence|computer-controlled]] units that periodically [[Spawning (video games)|spawn]] in groups and march along set paths toward their enemy's base, which is heavily guarded by defensive structures. Players can influence these units by eliminating enemy waves or supporting their own, affecting lane control and map pressure. This type of [[Multiplayer video game|multiplayer]] [[Online game|online video games]] originated as a subgenre of [[real-time strategy]] (RTS); however, most of the traditional RTS elements, such as building construction and unit production, were removed in favor of a more focused [[Player versus player|player-versus-player]] experience. The genre blends elements of [[real-time strategy]], [[Role-playing video game|role-playing]], and [[Action game|action games]], combining strategic depth with individual character progression and fast-paced combat.

The first widely accepted game in the genre was [[Aeon of Strife]], a fan-made custom map released in 2002 for ''[[StarCraft (video game)|StarCraft]],'' in which four players each control a single powerful unit and, aided by weak computer-controlled units, compete against a computer-controlled enemy force, which is initially stronger.<ref name="getdota">{{cite web|title=Frequently Asked Questions|url=http://www.getdota.com/faq|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101111183559/http://www.getdota.com/faq|archive-date=11 November 2010|publisher=GetDota.com|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> ''[[Defense of the Ancients]]'' (''DotA'') was created in 2003 by the ''Warcraft III'' [[Mod (video games)|modding]] community for ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos]]'' and its expansion, ''[[Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne|The Frozen Throne]],'' with a map based on ''AoS. DotA'' was one of the first major titles to establish the core mechanics of the MOBA genre, serving as a direct inspiration for later titles, and the first MOBA for which sponsored tournaments were held.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Walbridge|first=Michael|title=Analysis: Defense of the Ancients - An Underground Revolution|url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/109814/Analysis_Defense_of_the_Ancients__An_Underground_Revolution.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510135818/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/109814/Analysis_Defense_of_the_Ancients__An_Underground_Revolution.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 May 2012|access-date=2020-09-05|website=www.gamasutra.com|date=12 June 2008|language=en}}</ref> <!-- sorted by release date --> It was followed by two [[spiritual successor]]s, ''[[League of Legends]]'' (2009) and ''[[Heroes of Newerth]]'' (2010), a standalone sequel, ''[[Dota 2]]'' (2013), and other games in the genre, including ''[[Smite (video game)|Smite]]'' (2014) and ''[[Heroes of the Storm]]'' (2015).<ref>{{Cite web|title=How Warcraft 3's modding community paved the way for League of Legends and Dota 2|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/warcraft-iii/warcraft-3-mods-dota-league-of-legends|access-date=2020-09-06|website=PCGamesN|date=26 March 2018 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.progamerreview.com/best-moba-games/|title=Best Modern MOBA Games – LoL, Dota 2, HotS & Smite Compared|last1=Amstrup|first1=Johannes|last2=ersen|date=2017-09-15|website=Pro Gamer Reviews|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-19}}</ref>

Through the years, the MOBA genre has played a significant role in the rise of competitive [[esports]]. By the early 2010s, the genre had established itself as a major component of the esports landscape, with prize pools reaching over [[United States dollar|US$]]60 million in 2018, accounting for 40% of the total esports prize pools that year. Major esports professional tournaments are held in venues that can hold tens of thousands of spectators and are streamed online. A strong fanbase has opened up the opportunity for sponsorship and advertising, eventually leading the genre to become a global cultural phenomenon.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Huda |first1=Irfan Nabil |last2=Salehudin |first2=Imam |title=Escapism, family and friends, and social interactions: How watching esports increases gaming and in-game purchase intentions |journal=Jurnal Manajemen Dan Pemasaran Jasa |date=26 March 2024 |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=1–22 |doi=10.25105/jmpj.v17i1.18463 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Gameplay ==
[[File:Map of MOBA.svg|thumb|A generic map layout popular in MOBA games. Yellow lines are the "lanes" where the action is focused. Blue and red dots are the "towers", the main line of defense for both teams. Green area is the jungle. Two light-colored areas are the teams' bases which encompass the blue and red corners, the structures upon which destruction results in victory.]]

Each match starts with two opposing teams, typically with five players each. Players work together as a team to achieve the ultimate victory condition, which is to destroy their enemy's base whilst protecting their own.<ref name=":11">{{Cite web|date=2013-08-01|title=How MOBAs Took Over Gaming|url=https://me.ign.com/en/pc/70142/feature/how-mobas-took-over-gaming|access-date=2020-09-05|website=IGN Middle East|language=en-ae}}</ref> Both teams usually have their main structures placed on opposite sides of the battlefield. The first team to destroy the opponents' main structure wins the match,<ref name=":11" /> though some games have the option of different victory conditions.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Crystal Scar &#124; League of Legends|url=http://dominion.leagueoflegends.com/overview-dominion|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140708150148/http://dominion.leagueoflegends.com/overview-dominion|archive-date=8 July 2014|access-date=23 December 2015|publisher=Dominion.leagueoflegends.com|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Destroying other structures in the enemy's base may provide other benefits. Defensive structures, usually automatic "towers", are in place to prevent this. Each team is assisted by relatively weak computer-controlled units, called "minions", that periodically spawn in groups at both bases, marching down predefined paths (called "lanes") toward the enemy base. While minions naturally engage opposing forces, players can support them to increase their effectiveness in pushing through enemy defenses.<ref>{{cite web | last=Leahy | first=Brian |url=http://www.shacknews.com/onearticle.x/66007 |title=Dota Explained and How You Can Play it Now |date=13 October 2010 |publisher=Shacknews.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101115130020/http://www.shacknews.com/onearticle.x/66007 |archive-date=15 November 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Esports primer: League of Legends |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/esports-lol-primer-idUSFLM1tj2jd |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310080830/https://www.reuters.com/article/esports-lol-primer-idUSFLM1tj2jd |url-status=dead |archive-date=2021-03-10 |website=WebArchive |access-date=4 June 2025}}</ref> There are typically three "lanes" on the battlefield that serve as primary paths between bases. The lanes are known as top, middle and bottom lane, or, in gamer shorthand – "top", "mid" and "bot". Between the lanes is an uncharted area called "jungle".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-09-22|title=Proving Grounds: The Geography of the MOBA Map|url=https://killscreen.com/themeta/proving-grounds-geography-moba-map/|access-date=2020-09-06|website=The Meta|language=en-US}}</ref> The "jungle" is home to neutral monsters hostile to both teams and appear in marked locations on the map known as "camps".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gies|first=Arthur|date=2017-08-02|title=The Normal Person's Guide to Watching Competitive Dota 2 (2017 Edition)|url=https://www.polygon.com/2017/8/2/16073588/the-normal-persons-guide-to-watching-competitive-dota-2-2017-edition|access-date=2020-09-07|website=Polygon|language=en}}</ref> Defeating these monsters grants various benefits to the players and their team, such as growth in power, temporary [[Buff (video gaming)|buffs]], or assistance in pushing the lane. Effective control over lanes and jungle objectives is crucial for maintaining map pressure and dictating the flow of the match.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|date=2018-10-17|title=Roshan Dota 2 Guide|url=https://pages.firstblood.io/pages/blog/dota-2/roshan-dota-2-guide/|access-date=2019-09-25|website=FirstBlood®|language=en-US|archive-date=25 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925110057/https://pages.firstblood.io/pages/blog/dota-2/roshan-dota-2-guide/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":9" />

The games are usually played on a battlefield shown from an [[Isometric video game graphics|isometric perspective]], but certain MOBAs are played from a [[Third-person (video games)|third-person]] or [[Side-scrolling video game|side-view]] perspective.<ref name=":2" /> The battlefield is represented in the interface by the [[mini-map]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Where should we place the mini map?|url=https://www.gamasutra.com/blogs/JacekSliwinski/20130121/185119/Where_should_we_place_the_mini_map.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130124090356/http://gamasutra.com/blogs/JacekSliwinski/20130121/185119/Where_should_we_place_the_mini_map.php|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 January 2013|access-date=2020-09-05|website=www.gamasutra.com|date=21 January 2013|language=en}}</ref>

A player controls a single powerful in-game unit, known as a "hero" or "champion," with a distinctive set of abilities and a unique playstyle.<ref name=":5" /> Heroes gain [[Experience point|experience points]] and gold by being near defeated enemies or delivering the killing blow. Experience allows them to level up and enhance abilities, while gold is used to purchase items that improve their power. Most heroes have four abilities that can be upgraded as they progress. If a hero [[Life (gaming)|runs out of health points]] and dies, they are removed from active play until a [[Spawning (video games)|respawn]] timer counts down to zero, at which point the hero respawns in their base. The respawn time increases as the game progresses and heroes level up.<ref name="herodeath">{{cite web |url=http://www.playdota.com/learn/survival |title=Basic Survival – Learn Dota |publisher=PlayDota.com |access-date=28 October 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120902023750/http://www.playdota.com/learn/survival |archive-date=2 September 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Heroes typically fall into one of several roles, such as tank, damage dealer, and support, each with unique designs, strengths, and weaknesses.<ref name=":5" /> MOBAs typically offer a large number of [[Game balance|viable]] playable heroes – ''League of Legends'', for instance, began with 40, and added characters over time, reaching 100 in 2012 and 150 in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anniversary Mural & Gifts|url=https://nexus.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/2019/10/anniversary-mural-gifts/|access-date=2020-09-07|website=nexus.leagueoflegends.com|date=17 October 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Augustine | first=Rob | url=http://www.pcgamer.com/introducing-league-of-legends-100th-champion-jayce-the-defender-of-tomorrow/ | title=Introducing League of Legends' 100th champion: Jayce, the Defender of Tomorrow | website=PC Gamer | date=3 July 2012 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161109152828/http://www.pcgamer.com/introducing-league-of-legends-100th-champion-jayce-the-defender-of-tomorrow/ | archive-date=9 November 2016 | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-07-24|title=Yone announced as League's 150th champion: Abilities, release date, more|url=https://www.dexerto.com/league-of-legends/yone-announced-as-leagues-150th-champion-abilities-release-date-more-1396725/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=Dexerto|language=en}}</ref> This contributes to the game's strategic depth and learning curve as players must be aware of an increasing list of available characters. Choosing the right character is a skill, requiring players to evaluate available options and select one that fits their skill set, team composition, and opposing picks.<ref name=":3" /> Players often find a hero they excel at, referred to as a "main", and familiarize themselves with the remaining roster.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Master the hot new mobile game Arena of Valor with our tips|url=https://www.redbull.com/int-en/arena-of-valor-tips|access-date=2020-09-05|website=Red Bull|date=30 August 2017 |language=en}}</ref> Each hero is limited in the roles they can fulfill. No single hero is supposed to be powerful enough to win the game without team support. This creates a strong emphasis on teamwork and cooperation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gogamingkits.com/why-moba-games-force-players-to-work-together/|title=Why MOBA Games Force Players to Work Together: The Hero Limitation Design Philosophy| website= gogamingkits.com}}</ref> The genre rewards players that are capable of cooperating with teammates to execute an effective strategy, enabling full potential of their individual abilities and mechanical skills.<ref name=":6">{{Cite arXiv|last1=Silva|first1=Victor do Nascimento|last2=Chaimowicz|first2=Luiz|date=2017-05-30|title=MOBA: a New Arena for Game AI|eprint=1705.10443 |class=cs|language=en}}</ref>

Each player typically receives a small amount of gold per second during the course of the game. Moderate amounts of gold are rewarded for killing hostile computer-controlled units and larger amounts are rewarded for killing enemy heroes. Gold is used by heroes to buy a variety of different items that range in price and impact. For the most part, this involves improving the combat viability of the hero, although there may be other items that support the hero or team as a whole in different ways.<ref name="DOTA2gameplay">{{cite web |last=Biessener |first=Adam |url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2010/10/13/dota-2-announced-details.aspx |title=Valve's New Game Announced, Detailed: Dota 2 |date=13 October 2010 |publisher=[[Game Informer]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101016155010/http://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2010/10/13/dota-2-announced-details.aspx |archive-date=16 October 2010 |url-status=live |access-date=20 October 2010 }}</ref> As the heroes of each team get stronger, they can use multiple strategies to gain an advantage. These strategies can include securing objectives, killing enemy heroes, and gaining levels by defeating computer-controlled units. As a team grows stronger, they gain greater control over the map, apply more pressure on the opponent, and become more capable of dismantling the enemy's defenses and structures, ultimately leading to the destruction of their base.<ref name=":3" />

=== Character classes and roles ===
In most MOBAs, [[Player character|playable characters]] have assigned classes such as [[Tank (gaming)|"tank"]], "bruiser", "marksman", "mage", "fighter", "assassin", "support" and [[Healer (video games)|"healer"]], with each classification denoting various different skill sets and proficiencies.<ref name=":10" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-03-27|title=Heroes of the Storm: Hero Roles Expanded|url=https://www.player.one/heroes-storm-patch-hero-roles-expanded-125044|access-date=2020-09-05|website=Player.One|language=en}}</ref> During the match, characters can be played in roles such as "carry", "support" and [[Ganking|"ganker"]]; however, the number and type of roles can differ depending on the game.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4s9yCwAAQBAJ&q=The+Effects+of+Gameplay+on+Leadership+Behaviors%3A+An+Empirical+Study+on+Leadership+Behaviors+and+Roles+in+Multiplayer+Online+Battle+Arena+Games&pg=PA142|title=Transactions on Computational Science XXVI: Special Issue on Cyberworlds and Cybersecurity|last=Gavrilova|first=Nuangjumnong|date=2016-01-22|publisher=Springer|isbn=9783662492475|pages=147|language=en|chapter=The Effects of Gameplay on Leadership Behaviors: An Empirical Study on Leadership Behaviors and Roles in Multiplayer Online Battle Arena Games}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Ng|first1=Patrick|last2=Nesbitt|first2=Keith|last3=Blackmore|first3=Karen|date=2015-02-05|chapter=Sound Improves Player Performance in a Multiplayer Online Battle Arena Game|title=Artificial Life and Computational Intelligence|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science|volume=8955 |language=en|publisher=Springer, Cham|pages=166–174|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-14803-8_13|isbn=9783319148021}}</ref> The carry role is expected to scale and itemize themselves to do the most damage against enemy characters and objectives, but may also require protection and assistance from their team members.<ref name=":0" /> Supports assist their team with abilities that aid allies and disable enemies, rather than dealing damage directly. Some supports have healing abilities which can be vital factor in the team composition's success, giving health and sustenance to their allies while limiting the enemy's options in terms of play patterns.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://dignitas.gg/articles/blogs/Heroes-Of-The-Storm/13444/understanding-roles-in-hots|title=Understanding Roles in HotS – Articles – Dignitas|website=dignitas.gg|date=27 February 2019|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> Ganker roles are flexible, as they have both carry and support skills that are used to disrupt and eliminate enemies, thus giving their teammates an advantage over their opponents.<ref name=":0" /> Gankers can "act as a strategist, decision-maker or supporter depending on the team's needs."<ref name=":0" /> Player roles can be classified by the particular lane they are focusing on, such as "top laner", "mid laner", and "bottom laner",<ref name=":10">{{Cite web|date=2020-03-20|title=League of Legends Roles and Champion Positions|url=https://www.mobachampion.com/blog/league-of-legends-slang-terms-and-meanings/|access-date=2020-09-05|website=MOBA Champion|language=en-US}}</ref> or by their role in a teamfight, such as "frontliner", "damage dealer", "healer", "flex", and the "offlaner".<ref name=":1" />

=== Resemblance to other genres ===
[[File:Vainglory Halcyon Fold map.jpg|thumb|The Halcyon Fold map from the game ''[[Vainglory (video game)|Vainglory]]'' features a single lane connecting the two team bases, and the "jungle" underbrush beneath the lane.]]
As a fusion of [[real-time strategy]] (RTS), [[Role-playing video game|role-playing]], and [[action game]]s, MOBAs have many elements of established genres while still offering unique gameplay. In general, the design philosophy of the MOBA genre has moved away from constructing structures, army building, and controlling additional units in favor of hero-centric gameplay.<ref name=":6" /> However, some MOBA games have certain heroes that control a few specialized units,<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Lost Vikings – Heroes of the Storm|url=http://us.battle.net/heroes/en/heroes/the-lost-vikings/|access-date=2019-09-24|website=us.battle.net|language=en-us}}</ref> but not on the massive scale commonly found in RTS games.<ref name=":6" /> Much like real-time strategy games, structures and base defense play a crucial role in MOBAs, with the victory condition often being the destruction of the main structure in the enemy base. Players can find various friendly and enemy units on the map assisting each team. However, these units are computer-controlled and players usually do not control their movement or [[Spawning (video games)|creation]]. Instead of building them, players rely on these units to move along the map's lanes.

Many defining elements of the action genre<ref name="NGen15">{{cite magazine|date=March 1996|title=The Next Generation 1996 Lexicon A to Z|magazine=[[Next Generation (magazine)|Next Generation]]|publisher=[[Imagine Media]]|issue=15|pages=28–42|quote=Action game - A game characterized by simple action and response gameplay. ... the defining characteristic is that enemies and obstacles are overcome by 'physical' means, rather than involved intellectual problem solving.}}</ref><ref name="AdRol2006" /> are represented in MOBA games. Players with better mechanical skills and quick reaction times typically excel relative to their peers. MOBAs often have a strong focus on [[Micromanagement (gameplay)|micromanagement]], involving mechanical abilities such as positioning, dodging, use of [[Combo (video games)|combo]] attacks, [[Glossary of video game terms#kiting|kiting]], prediction and target selection.<ref name=":6" /> Direction-targeted abilities, or "skillshots", require precise aim and good timing in order to hit an enemy.<ref>{{Cite web|last=PicklePantsLOL|date=2020-06-30|title=How to Hit Skill Shots more Effectively {{!}} Day 25/30|url=https://medium.com/@PicklePantsLoL/how-to-hit-skill-shots-more-effectively-d1dbbce69815|access-date=2020-09-08|website=Medium|language=en}}</ref>

The MOBA genre resembles role-playing games (RPGs) in gameplay, though the MOBA genre focuses on the multiplayer battle in the arena-like environment, whereas RPGs typically revolve around a single-player story and exploration of different locations.<ref name="AdRol347">[[#AdRol|Adams, Rollings 2003]], p. 347</ref><ref name="AdRol2006">[[#adamsrollings_2006|Adams, Rollings 2006]]</ref> Some key features of MOBAs, such as control over one specific character in a party, growth in power over time, learning new thematic abilities, leveling and accumulation of experience points,<ref>{{Cite web|title=What you need to know about the experience in Dota 2 written by Artem Uarabei {{!}} Click-Storm|url=https://click-storm.com/en/articles/6795/|access-date=2019-09-25|website=Click-Storm.com|language=en}}</ref> usage of the [[Magic (gaming)|mana]] resource,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jacobacci|first=Kara|date=2016-04-22|title=Mana - Less Heroes in the ARTS MOBA Genre|url=https://esportsedition.com/dota-2/mana-less-heroes-in-the-arts-moba-genre/|access-date=2020-09-08|website=Esports Edition|language=en-US}}</ref> equipment and inventory management,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://na.leagueoflegends.com/en/game-info/items/|title=Items {{!}} League of Legends|website=na.leagueoflegends.com|access-date=2019-09-25}}</ref> completing quests,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.esportstalk.com/blog/5-most-important-heroes-of-the-storm-objectives-10213/|title=The 5 Most Important Heroes of the Storm Objectives|date=2018-11-21|website=EsportsTalk.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-25}}</ref> and fighting with powerful [[Boss (video gaming)|boss]] monsters,<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9">{{Cite web|url=http://team-dignitas.net/articles/blogs/Heroes-Of-The-Storm/11768/heroes-of-the-storm-how-to-fully-utilize-mercenary-camps|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030105304/http://team-dignitas.net/articles/blogs/Heroes-Of-The-Storm/11768/heroes-of-the-storm-how-to-fully-utilize-mercenary-camps|url-status=usurped|archive-date=30 October 2017|title=Heroes of the Storm: How to Fully Utilize Boss and Mercenary Camps – Articles – Dignitas|website=team-dignitas.net|date=27 October 2017|access-date=2019-09-25}}</ref> are also typical of role-playing games.

== History ==

=== Origins ===
The 1989 [[Sega Genesis|Mega Drive/Genesis]] game ''[[Herzog Zwei]]'' has variously been cited either as a precursor to,<ref name="GameAxis">''GameAxis Unwired'', [https://books.google.com/books?id=vuoDAAAAMBAJ&dq=herzog+dota&pg=PA52 p. 52], December 2008, [[SPH Magazines]], ISSN 0219-872X</ref><ref name="MCV">Greg Lockley (3 June 2014), [http://www.mcvuk.com/news/read/moba-the-story-so-far/0133335 MOBA: The story so far] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427151821/http://www.mcvuk.com/news/read/moba-the-story-so-far/0133335 |date=27 April 2017 }}, [[MCV (magazine)|MCV]]</ref> or an early example of,
the MOBA genre.<ref name="destructoid">{{cite web |url=http://www.destructoid.com/review-airmech-242461.phtml |last=Brown |first=Fraser |title=Like Macross without the drama |date=15 January 2013 |access-date=19 January 2013 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130119043712/http://www.destructoid.com/review-airmech-242461.phtml |archive-date=19 January 2013 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="gamesradar">Andrew Groen (7 March 2012), [http://www.gamesradar.com/ask-gr-anything-whats-moba/ Ask GR Anything: What's a MOBA?] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630043636/http://www.gamesradar.com/ask-gr-anything-whats-moba/ |date=30 June 2017 }}, [[GamesRadar]]</ref> It uses a similar formula, where each player controls a single command unit in one of two opposing sides on a battlefield.<ref name="MCV"/><ref name="gamesradar"/><ref name="GameAxis"/> ''Herzog Zwei''{{'}}s influence is apparent in several later MOBA games such as ''[[Guilty Gear 2: Overture]]'' (2007)<ref>{{Cite web|date=2009-05-08|title=Herzog Zwei (or: How I Learned To Stop Worrying And Love Console Multiplayer)|url=https://venturebeat.com/2009/05/08/herzog-zwei-or-how-i-learned-to-stop-worrying-and-love-console-multiplayer/|access-date=2020-09-20|website=VentureBeat|language=en-US}}</ref> and ''[[AirMech]]'' (2012).<ref name="destructoid"/> ''Herzog Zwei'' was also cited as an inspiration to the developers of ''[[Warcraft: Orcs & Humans|Warcraft]]'' and ''[[StarCraft (video game)|Starcraft]].''<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-06-04|title=The Essential 50 Part 31: Herzog Zwei|url=http://www.1up.com/features/essential-50-herzog-zwei|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120614033131/http://www.1up.com/features/essential-50-herzog-zwei|url-status=dead|archive-date=2012-06-14|access-date=2020-09-20|website=[[1Up Network]]|via=[[Internet Archive]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2011-11-22|title=The Origin of Realtime Strategy Games on the PC|url=http://above-the-garage.com/rblts/vie16b.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111122065508/http://above-the-garage.com/rblts/vie16b.htm|archive-date=22 November 2011|access-date=2020-09-20}}</ref>

1998's ''[[Future Cop: LAPD]]'' has a strategic "Precinct Assault" mode similar to ''Herzog Zwei'' in which players can actively fight alongside generated non-player units.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ign.com/articles/1998/12/15/future-cop-lapd|title=Future Cop: LAPD|date=14 December 1998|publisher=IGN|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151224105144/http://www.ign.com/articles/1998/12/15/future-cop-lapd|archive-date=24 December 2015|url-status=live|access-date=23 December 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamerevolution.com/review/future-cop-lapd|title=Future Cop L.A.P.D. Review|date=1 September 1998|publisher=Gamerevolution.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151224104032/http://www.gamerevolution.com/review/future-cop-lapd|archive-date=24 December 2015|url-status=live|access-date=23 December 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref>
This could be regarded as the first example of MOBA gameplay, depending on the definition of the genre.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lopuszanski |first=Stefan |date=2019 |title=It's Mods All The Way Down |language=en |doi=10.13140/RG.2.2.25818.08644 |journal=ResearchGate}}</ref> The Windows version of ''Future Cop: LAPD'' allows online competitive play.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-06-15 |title=Herzog Zwei |url=https://classicreload.com/genesis-herzog-zwei.html |access-date=2020-09-20 |website=ClassicReload.com |language=en |quote=The multiplayer mode is only possible via a split-screen setup, in which the competing players can observe the other's activity, making discreet maneuvers or surprise attacks difficult to execute.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-05-23 |title=Future Cop: LAPD |url=https://www.play-old-pc-games.com/2014/05/23/future-cop-lapd/ |access-date=2019-01-17 |website=Play Old PC Games |language=en-US}}</ref><!-- Aeon of Strife (AoS) -->

In the same year, [[Blizzard Entertainment]] released its best-selling real-time strategy game ''StarCraft'' (1998) with a suite of game editing tools called ''[[StarEdit]]''. These tools allowed players to design and create custom maps with non-standard rules and gameplay, such as [[Aeon of Strife]]. Some of the key features introduced in the map became the foundation of the newborn genre.<ref>{{Cite web |title=David Dannelly Portfolio - The Origin of the MOBA: Aeon of Strife and Defense of the Ancients |url=https://daviddannelly.com/blog/zjYm/the-origin-of-the-moba-aeon-of-strife-and-defense-of-the-ancients |access-date=2026-09-02 |website=daviddannelly.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="eurogamer">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-08-16-the-story-of-dota-article|title=The Story of DOTA|last=Dean|first=Paul|date=16 August 2011|work=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=Gamer Network|access-date=6 April 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108042709/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-08-16-the-story-of-dota-article|archive-date=8 November 2016|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In Aeon of Strife, players controlled a single powerful hero unit fighting along three lanes which were protected by defensive towers.<ref name=eurogamer/><ref name=themittani>{{cite web| url=http://themittani.com/features/dota-2-history-lesson?page=0%2C0| title=Dota 2: A History Lesson| last=Dimirti| publisher=The Mittani| date=22 July 2013| access-date=24 August 2013| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211054041/http://themittani.com/features/dota-2-history-lesson?page=0%2C0| archive-date=11 December 2013| df=dmy-all}}</ref>

=== Establishing the genre: 2000s ===
In 2002, Blizzard released ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos]]'' (WC3), with the accompanying ''[[Warcraft III World Editor]]''. Both the multiplayer online battle arena and [[tower defense]] subgenres took substantive shape within the ''WC3'' modding community. A [[Mod (video games)|modder]] named Eul began converting Aeon of Strife into the ''Warcraft III'' engine, calling the map ''[[Defense of the Ancients]]'' (''DotA''). Eul significantly expanded the complexity of play from the original Aeon of Strife mod. Shortly after creating the custom ''DotA'' map, Eul left the modding scene. With no clear successor, ''Warcraft III'' modders created a variety of maps based on ''DotA'' and featuring different heroes. In 2003, after the release of ''[[WarCraft III: The Frozen Throne]]'', a map creator named Meian<ref name="getdota" /> created a ''DotA'' variant closely modeled on Eul's map, but combining heroes from the many other versions of ''DotA'' that existed at the time. Called ''DotA: Allstars'', it was inherited after a few months by a modder called Steve "Guinsoo" Feak, and under his guidance it became the dominant map of the genre. After more than a year of maintaining the ''DotA: Allstars'' map, with the impending release of an update that significantly changed the map layout, Guinsoo left the development to his adjutant Neichus in the year 2005.<ref name="getdota" /> After some weeks of development and some versions released, the latter turned over responsibility to a modder named [[IceFrog]], who implemented substantial changes to the mechanics that deepened its complexity and capacity for innovative gameplay. The changes conducted by IceFrog proved popular with the community and the number of users on the ''Dota: Allstars'' forum reportedly peaked at over one million.<ref name="themittani" /> ''DotA'' is widely regarded as the most significant influence on the MOBA genre, shaping its core mechanics and inspiring the development of numerous titles in the years to come.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2013/9/2/4672920/moba-dota-arts-a-brief-introduction-to-gamings-biggest-most|title=MOBA, DOTA, ARTS: A brief introduction to gaming's biggest, most impenetrable genre|last=Funk|first=John|date=2013-09-02|website=Polygon|language=en|access-date=2019-11-24}}</ref>

=== Mainstream popularity: 2008–present ===
By 2008, the popularity of ''DotA'' had attracted commercial attention.<ref name="1up-dota">{{cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Thierry |date=1 September 2009 |url=http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3175835 |title=Clash of The DOTAs |publisher=[[1UP.com]] |access-date=21 October 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111128151953/http://www.1up.com/features/clash-dotas-league-legends-heroes |archive-date=28 November 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Since the format was tied to the ''Warcraft'' property, developers began to work on their own "''DOTA''-style" video games.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|date=2014-09-01|title=The history of MOBAs: From mod to sensation|url=https://venturebeat.com/2014/09/01/the-history-of-mobas-from-mod-to-sensation/|access-date=2020-09-09|website=VentureBeat|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Crecente|first=Brian|title=League of Legends is now 10 years old. This is the story of its birth.|language=en-US|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/video-games/2019/10/27/league-legends-is-now-years-old-this-is-story-its-birth/|access-date=2020-09-04|issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Nemikan |url=http://gaming.icrontic.com/reviews/dota-reborn-three-games-inspired-by-the-legendary-wc3-mod/ |title=DOTA reborn: Three games inspired by the legendary WC3 mod |publisher=Icrontic.com |date=21 September 2009 |access-date=17 November 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826010826/http://icrontic.com/article/dota-reborn-three-games-inspired-by-the-legendary-wc3-mod |archive-date=26 August 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> A [[Adobe Flash|Flash]] web game, named ''[[Minions (video game)|Minions]],'' was created by [[Kixeye|The Casual Collective]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://jayisgames.com/archives/2008/11/minions.php |title=Minions |author=Psychotronic |date=30 November 2008 |access-date=7 November 2012 |publisher=jayisgames.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107114907/http://jayisgames.com/archives/2008/11/minions.php |archive-date=7 November 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> [[Gas Powered Games]] released the first stand-alone commercial title in the genre, ''[[Demigod (video game)|Demigod]]'' (2009).<ref>{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=Miguel |url=http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/gas-powered-games-project/854109p1.html |title=Demigod |date=21 February 2008 |access-date=20 November 2010 |publisher=Gamespy.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120907175611/http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/gas-powered-games-project/854109p1.html |archive-date=7 September 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> In late 2009, [[Riot Games]]' debut title ''[[League of Legends]]'' was released. It was initially designed by Steve Feak, one of the original creators of ''DotA: Allstars,'' who went on to apply many of the mechanics and lessons he learned from the mod.<ref name="1up-guinsoo2">{{cite web|last=Perez|first=Daniel|date=January 16, 2009|title=Previews; We talk with new developer Riot Games about its strategy/RPG hybrid and the lead designer's Warcraft roots.|url=http://www.1up.com/do/previewPage?cId=3172308&p=1|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111130044838/http://www.1up.com/previews/league-of-legends|archive-date=November 30, 2011|access-date=February 7, 2009|publisher=[[1UP.com]]}}</ref><ref name="gameriotdotagenre">{{cite web|author=Arirang|date=3 October 2009|title=A Look at the Future of Dota and the AoS Genre.|url=http://wowriot.gameriot.com/blogs/The-Ohcee/DOTA-A-Look-at-the-Future-of-Dota-and-the-AoS-Genre|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826034014/http://www.gameriot.com/offline/|archive-date=26 August 2012|access-date=19 October 2010|publisher=GameRiot.com|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Riot began to refer to the game's genre as a multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA).<ref name="gamasutra">{{cite web|url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/the-valve-way-gabe-newell-and-erik-johnson-speak|title=The Valve Way: Gabe Newell And Erik Johnson Speak|first=Christian|last=Nutt|work=Game Developer |date=29 August 2011|access-date=24 August 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023063739/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/6471/the_valve_way_gabe_newell_and_.php?page=3|archive-date=23 October 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Also in 2009, IceFrog, who had continued to develop ''DotA: Allstars'', was hired by [[Valve Corporation|Valve]], in order to design a sequel to the original map.<ref name="themittani" />

the ''DotA'' trademark.<ref>{{cite web |author=Josh Augustine |url=http://www.pcgamer.com/2010/08/17/riot-games-dev-counter-files-dota-trademark/ |title=Riot Games' dev counter-files "DotA" trademark ==== Next-generation wave and market saturation ====
During the last half of the 2010s, [[video game developer]]s and [[Video game publisher|publishers]], following the success of ''League of Legends'' and ''Dota 2'', tried to be part of the next-generation MOBA wave by putting their own twist in the genre,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ag.hyperxgaming.com/article/3709/battlerite-review---moba-battles-done-right|title=Battlerite Review: All the teamfights you'd ever want in a MOBA, minus the MOBA structure.|website=AllGamers|date=12 January 2018 |language=en|access-date=2019-09-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/paragon-preview-epic-games-re-energises-moba-classic-shooter-elements-unique-twists-1544568|title=Paragon preview: Epic Games re-energises the MOBA with classic shooter elements and unique twists|date=2016-02-18|website=International Business Times UK|language=en|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/ncsoft-announces-master-x-master-a-tag-team-action-moba/|title=NCsoft announces Master X Master, a tag-team "action MOBA"|last=Chalk|first=Andy|date=2016-01-27|website=PC Gamer|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://in.ign.com/preview/4281/what-do-igns-moba-experts-think-of-arena-of-fate|title=IGN: Arena of Fate has the 20-minute time limit on each match, and it's all about scoring enough points before that timer runs out|date=2014-06-26|website=IGN India|language=en|access-date=2019-09-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamespot.com/gigantic/user-reviews/2200-12737495/|title=GameSpot: Gigantic is the new free fast-paced hero shooter MOBA|website=GameSpot|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-26}}</ref> releasing games such as ''[[Battlerite]]'' (2017), and ''[[AirMech]]'' (2018). After years of development, many games which were supported by large publishers have not been fully released or their servers were shut down shortly after release. The most notable examples are ''[[Dawngate]]'' (2015){{efn|The number in brackets represents the year of official servers shut down.}} by [[Electronic Arts]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.engadget.com/2014/11/04/dawngate-shutting-down-in-90-days/|title=Dawngate shutting down in 90 days|website=Engadget|date=4 November 2014 |language=en|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> DC Comics-based [[Infinite Crisis (video game)|''Infinite Crisis'']] (2015) by [[Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment|Warner Bros.]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2015-06-02-warner-bros-shutting-down-infinite-crisis-only-2-months-after-launch|title=Warner Bros. shutting down Infinite Crisis only 2 months after launch|website=GamesIndustry.biz|date=2 June 2015 |language=en|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> ''[[Arena of Fate]]'' (2016) by [[Crytek Black Sea|Crytek]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.player.one/crysis-developer-crytek-shuts-down-all-two-studios-574984|title='Crysis' Developer Crytek Shuts Down All But Two Studios|date=2016-12-20|website=Player.One|language=en|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> ''[[Gigantic (video game)|Gigantic]]'' (2017) by [[Perfect World Entertainment]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/2018/1/31/16956254/gigantic-shutting-down-january-update-motiga|title=Gigantic gets final update, shutting down in July|last=McWhertor|first=Michael|date=2018-01-31|website=Polygon|language=en|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> ''[[Master X Master]]'' (2018) by [[NCSoft]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-11-17-ncsoft-will-shut-down-master-x-master-just-months-after-launch|title=NCsoft will shut down Master X Master just months after launch|website=GamesIndustry.biz|date=17 November 2017 |language=en|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> and ''[[Paragon (video game)|Paragon]]'' (2018) by [[Epic Games]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kotaku.com/after-fortnites-massive-success-epic-shuts-down-parago-1822460782|title=After Fortnite's Massive Success, Epic Shuts Down Paragon|last=Schreier|first=Jason|website=Kotaku|date=26 January 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-24}}</ref> 

The saturation of the market and the dominance of established titles contributed to the decline of many new MOBA attempts, as they struggled to retain player engagement and compete with the genre's leading games.

In 2024, Valve announced their second MOBA title, [[Deadlock (video game)|''Deadlock'']], after it was leaked by playtesters earlier that year.<ref name="Peters-2024">{{Cite news == Impact ==
[[File:League of Legends World Championship 2017 Finals.jpg|thumb|The [[2017 League of Legends World Championship|2017 ''League of Legends'' World Championship]] Finals held in the [[Beijing National Stadium]], China|alt=]]
<!-- eSports -->
In the original ''[[Defense of the Ancients]]'' (''DotA''), each player controls one powerful unit rather than a large army. While it still kept the large scale, core mechanics, and goals of the [[real-time strategy]] games, ''DotA'' attempted to avoid "clickfest" gameplay in which high [[actions per minute]] scores are mandatory for efficient playing, changing focus to the actual teamwork, coordination, and tactics. This made the [[Mod (video games)|mod]] highly popular, as its dynamic and unpredictable fights, complex map, and hero-centric gameplay creates a more competitive environment and opportunities for outplaying the enemy team.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=Crider|first=Michael|title=Why Are MOBA Games like League of Legends So Popular?|url=https://www.howtogeek.com/331389/why-are-moba-games-like-league-of-legends-so-popular/|access-date=2020-07-19|website=How-To Geek|date=6 November 2017 |language=en-US}}</ref> Over time, the multiplayer online battle arena genre grew steadily within [[esports]] tournaments, becoming a major part of the competitive gaming scene by the early 2010s. The genre has seen further growth in popularity since the year 2015 – among the top five esports with the largest prize pools, three have been MOBA titles for three years in row.{{citation needed|date=April 2021}} Distributed prize money in MOBA tournaments reached over [[United States dollar|US$]]54 million in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-12-25|title=The Top 10 Games of 2017, Based on Distributed Earnings|url=https://esportsobserver.com/top-ten-games-2017/|access-date=2020-09-22|website=The Esports Observer｜home of essential esports business news and insights|language=en-US}}</ref> A year later, prize pools continued to grow reaching over US$60 million, 40% of the year's total esports prize pools.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|last=Hurst|first=Taylor|date=2019-02-12|title=Esports Prize Pools: $155.9M (2018)|url=https://medium.com/konvoy/esports-prize-pools-155-9m-2018-ce1ff44bd41|access-date=2020-04-22|website=Medium|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-12-25|title=The 10 Biggest Esports of 2018 by Total Prize Pool|url=https://esportsobserver.com/10-biggest-prize-pools-2018/|access-date=2020-09-22|website=The Esports Observer｜home of essential esports business news and insights|language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[2018 League of Legends World Championship]]'' had the biggest prize pool out of all League of Legends esports championship finals, awarding almost $6.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 November 2022 |title=How Many People Play League of Legends & Average LoL Player Stats (2023) |url=https://headphonesaddict.com/league-of-legends-statistics/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=Headphones Addicts}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=LoL - Esports Viewership and Statistics |url=https://escharts.com/games/lol |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=Esports Charts}}</ref>

MOBAs are some of the largest audiences for games in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Most watched games on Twitch in 2017 – SullyGnome|url=https://sullygnome.com/games/2017/watched|access-date=2020-07-18|website=sullygnome.com}}</ref> Major esports professional tournaments are held in venues that can hold tens of thousands of spectators and are streamed online to millions of people by influencers and streamers such as [[Caedrel]] and [[OhnePixel]].<ref>{{Cite web|agency=Agence France-Presse|date=2017-11-05|title=Video game warriors do battle before 40,000 fans in China|url=https://technology.inquirer.net/68752/technology-games-china-video-games-esports-league-of-legends-birds-nest|access-date=2020-07-19|website=INQUIRER.net|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Webb|first=Kevin|title=More than 100 million people watched the 'League of Legends' World Championship, cementing its place as the most popular esport|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/league-of-legends-world-championship-100-million-viewers-2019-12|access-date=2020-07-19|website=Business Insider}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Boudreau|first=Ian|date=2019-08-26|title=The International 2019 was Twitch's most-watched Dota 2 event ever|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-international-2019-was-twitchs-most-watched-dota-2-event-ever/|access-date=2020-07-19|website=PC Gamer|language=en-US}}</ref> An active fanbase has opened up the opportunity for sponsorship and advertising, eventually leading the genre to become a global [[cultural phenomenon]].<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Meola|first=Andrew|title=The biggest companies sponsoring eSports teams and tournaments|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/top-esports-sponsors-gaming-sponsorships-2018-1|access-date=2020-09-25|website=Business Insider}}</ref>

A [[free-to-play]] business model, which is used by the largest MOBA titles, have contributed to the genre's overall popularity. Players are able to download and play [[AAA (video game industry)|AAA]]-quality games at no cost. These games are generating revenue by selling cosmetic elements, including skins, voice lines, customized mounts and announcers, but none of these give the functional gameplay advantages to the buyer. As of 2012, free-to-play MOBAs, such as ''League of Legends'', ''Dota 2'', ''Heroes of the Storm'', and ''Smite'' were among the most popular PC games.<ref>{{cite magazine | last = Gaudiosi | first = John | url = https://www.forbes.com/sites/johngaudiosi/2012/07/11/riot-games-league-of-legends-officially-becomes-most-played-pc-game-in-the-world | title = Riot Games' League Of Legends Officially Becomes Most Played PC Game In The World | date = July 11, 2012 | access-date = November 5, 2012 | magazine = [[Forbes]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-08-27|title=Q2 2019's Most Impactful PC Videogames: World Cup Boosts Fortnite, Blizzard on the Rise|url=https://esportsobserver.com/q2-2019-impact-index/|access-date=2020-09-22|website=The Esports Observer｜home of essential esports business news and insights|language=en-US}}</ref> The success in the genre has helped convince many [[video game publisher]]s to copy the free-to-play MOBA model.<ref>{{cite web | last = Drain | first = Brendan | url = http://massively.joystiq.com/2012/07/03/the-soapbox-league-of-legends-is-the-new-world-of-warcraft | title = The Soapbox: League of Legends is the new World of Warcraft | date = July 3, 2012 | access-date = November 5, 2012 | publisher = [[Joystiq]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150202024743/http://massively.joystiq.com/2012/07/03/the-soapbox-league-of-legends-is-the-new-world-of-warcraft | archive-date = February 2, 2015 | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Stapleton |first=Dan |url=http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/dota-2010/1224922p1.html |title=Valve: We Won't Charge for Dota 2 Heroes |date=June 1, 2012 |access-date=July 19, 2012 |publisher=[[GameSpy]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121030172013/http://pc.gamespy.com/pc/dota-2010/1224922p1.html |archive-date=October 30, 2012 |df=mdy }}</ref> SuperData Research reported that the genre generated over $2.5 billion of revenue in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=League of Legends Tops Free-to-Play Revenue Charts in 2017|url=https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/league-of-legends-top-free-to-play-revenue-charts-in-2017/|access-date=2020-07-18|website=GAMING|date=30 January 2018 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Forde|first1=Matthew|last2=Writer|first2=Staff|title=Moonton's Mobile Legends crosses $500 million in gross revenue|url=https://www.pocketgamer.biz/asia/news/72366/mobile-legends-500-million-usd-revenue/|access-date=2020-07-18|website=pocketgamer.biz|date=16 January 2020 }}</ref>

<!-- Cultural influence -->
Similar to [[fighting game]]s, MOBAs offer a large number of [[Game balance|viable]] [[player character]]s, each of which having distinctive abilities, strengths, and weaknesses. With numerous choices available, players can find the character that best fits their skills and preferences.<ref name=":3" /> Playable characters blend a variety of fantasy tropes and often reference [[popular culture]] and [[mythology]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Marshall|first=Cass|date=2019-12-05|title=Riot's new games are League of Legends' best asset (and biggest threat)|url=https://www.polygon.com/features/2019/12/5/20992482/riot-games-announcement-lore-storytelling-legends-of-runeterra-league-of-legends|access-date=2020-09-07|website=Polygon|language=en|quote="Now it has lore that’s legitimately worth reading, in a collection of genres ranging from Lovecraftian horror to knights and banners fantasy to pirate power struggles."}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-04-20|title=Blizzard's Worlds Collide When Heroes of the Storm™ Launches June 2|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20150420005352/en/Blizzard%E2%80%99s-Worlds-Collide-Heroes-Storm%E2%84%A2-Launches-June|access-date=2020-09-07|website=www.businesswire.com|language=en|quote="The free-to-play online team brawler brings together a diverse cast of iconic characters from Blizzard’s far-flung realms of science fiction and fantasy"}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The making of a Smite god: from mythology to main stage|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/smite/how-smite-s-gods-go-from-mythology-to-main-stage|access-date=2020-09-07|website=PCGamesN|date=27 November 2015 |language=en-GB|quote=Obviously we’re a game about mythology, so one of the things we look for is a mythological character that would be good to bring into the game}}</ref> One such figure commonly represented in MOBAs is [[Monkey King|Sun Wukong]], a legendary mythical figure from 16th-century China. Examples of representation of Sun Wukong in MOBAs in the form of playable characters include "Wukong" in ''League of Legends'', Samuro's "Monkey King" [[Skin (computing)|skin]] (custom outfit/costume) in ''Heroes of the Storm'', and "Monkey King" in ''DotA 2.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wukong, the Monkey King - League of Legends|url=https://www.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/champions/wukong/|access-date=2022-01-27|website=www.leagueoflegends.com|language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=S.E.H. @Gnub|first=Emil|title=Monkey King Samuro - Skin|url=https://nexuscompendium.com/skins/samuro-monkeyking|access-date=2022-01-27|website=The Nexus Compendium|language=en}}</ref>''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Monkey King|url=https://www.dota2.com/hero/monkeyking|access-date=2022-01-27|website=Dota 2}}</ref>

===Data analytics and match prediction===
Due to the large volume of matches played on a daily basis around the world and the relatively complicated nature of the genre,{{efn|''League of Legends'' alone had a reported 100 million active monthly players worldwide in 2016<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.riftherald.com/2016/9/13/12865314/monthly-lol-players-2016-active-worldwide | title = Number of players of selected eSports games worldwide as of August 2017 (in million) | date = 13 September 2016 | access-date=12 August 2018 | work = [[Rift Herald]]}}</ref> and an average of 27 million ''League of Legends'' games played per day reported in 2014.<ref>Sheer, Ian (January 27, 2014). "Player Tally for 'League of Legends' Surges". Wsj.com. Archived from the original on January 30, 2014. Retrieved January 31, 2014.</ref>}} MOBAs have become a popular target for the application of big data tools to predict match outcomes based on in-game factors such as hero kill/death/assist ratios, gold earned, time of a match, synergy with other players, team composition, and other, more advanced parameters.<ref>{{cite arXiv | title = Win Prediction in Esports: Mixed-Rank Match Prediction in Multi-player Online Battle Arena Games | date = 17 November 2017 |eprint = 1711.06498|last1 = Hodge|first1 = Victoria| last2 = Devlin | first2 = Sam | last3 = Sephton | first3 = Nick | last4 = Block | first4 = Florian | last5 = Drachen | first5 = Anders | last6 = Cowling | first6 = Peter | class = cs.AI }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.mobachampion.com/tier-list/ | title = LoL Tier List | date = 17 November 2017 | access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref>

=== Artificial intelligence in MOBAs ===
The use of [[Artificial intelligence in video games|artificial intelligence]] in MOBAs is an ongoing topic of research.<ref>{{ cite web | url = https://www.theverge.com/2018/8/28/17787610/openai-dota-2-bots-ai-lost-international-reinforcement-learning | title = OPENAI'S DOTA 2 DEFEAT IS STILL A WIN FOR ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE | date = 28 August 2018 | access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref> Similar to real-time strategy games, MOBAs provide a highly complex environment for AI because of their large amount of possible variables, states, and decisions. One of the first known research-based MOBA AI agents was published around 2015 for ''League of Legends''.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Silva|first1=Victor do Nascimento|last2=Chaimowicz|first2=Luiz|date=2017-06-08|title=On the Development of Intelligent Agents for MOBA Games|class=cs.AI|eprint=1706.02789}}</ref> The agent used influence maps to navigate the map and compute positioning risk. A similar agent to assist players was published in the same year.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Silva|first1=Victor do Nascimento|last2=Chaimowicz|first2=Luiz|date=2017-06-09|title=A Tutor Agent for MOBA Games|class=cs.AI|eprint=1706.02832}}</ref>

Two years later, artificial intelligence research laboratory [[OpenAI]] developed the AI project [[OpenAI Five]], which was first showcased at the ''Dota 2'' World Championship, [[The International 2017]], during a [[1v1]] demonstration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/8/14/16141938/dota-2-openai-bots-elon-musk-artificial-intelligence|title=My favorite game has been invaded by killer AI bots and Elon Musk hype|last=Savov|first=Vlad|date=2017-08-14|website=The Verge|access-date=2019-05-10}}</ref> In this demonstration, OpenAI Five faced off against [[Dendi (gamer)|Dendi]], a ''DotA'' player. In this 1v1, OpenAI Five defeated Dendi twice convincingly, with the first victory occurring before the five-minute mark and Dendi conceding before ninety seconds had passed in the second match.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sottek|first=T. C.|date=2017-08-11|title=The world's best Dota 2 players just got destroyed by a killer AI from Elon Musk's startup|url=https://www.theverge.com/2017/8/11/16137388/dota-2-dendi-open-ai-elon-musk|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The Verge|language=en}}</ref> OpenAI returned to [[The International 2018]], this time fielding an entire team of five AI players in two games against professional players, but ultimately losing both games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2018/08/24/openai_bots_eliminated_dota_2/|title=Game over, machines: Humans defeat OpenAI bots once again at video games Olympics|last=at 07:04|first=Katyanna Quach 24 Aug 2018|website=www.theregister.co.uk|language=en|access-date=2019-05-10}}</ref> Despite this loss, OpenAI continued to work to improve OpenAI Five, and the project's advancement soon became evident: one year later, at [[The International 2019]], OpenAI Five defeated The International 2018-winner [[OG (esports)|OG]] in a limited version of ''Dota 2'', becoming the first artificial intelligence system to beat the reigning world champion team at a video game.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Statt|first=Nick|date=2019-04-13|title=OpenAI's Dota 2 AI steamrolls world champion e-sports team with back-to-back victories|url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/4/13/18309459/openai-five-dota-2-finals-ai-bot-competition-og-e-sports-the-international-champion|access-date=2022-01-28|website=The Verge|language=en}}</ref>

The {{Nihongo foot|'''Nintendo Switch'''|ニンテンドースイッチ|Nintendō Suitchi|lead=yes|group=lower-alpha|extra=Nintendo branded the console in Japan in its English name.}} is a <!-- Please do not add "hybrid" here, as it is already stated later in this paragraph. --> [[video game console]] developed by [[Nintendo]] and released worldwide in most regions on March 3, 2017. Released in the middle of the [[Eighth generation of video game consoles|eighth generation of home consoles]], the Switch succeeded the [[Wii U]] and competed with [[Sony Interactive Entertainment|Sony]]'s [[PlayStation 4]] and [[Microsoft]]'s [[Xbox One]]; it also competes with the [[Ninth generation of video game consoles|ninth-generation consoles]], the [[PlayStation 5]] and [[Xbox Series X and Series S|Xbox Series X/S]].

The Switch is a [[Tablet computer#Gaming tablet|tablet]] that can either be [[docking station|docked]] for [[home video game console|home console]] use or used as a [[handheld game console|portable device]], making it a [[Video game console#Hybrid video game console|hybrid console]]. Its wireless [[Joy-Con]] controllers function as two halves of a standard controller and alternatively as individual controllers, featuring buttons, directional [[analog stick]]s for user input, motion sensing, and tactile feedback. A pair can attach to the sides of the console for handheld play, attach to a grip accessory to provide the form of a separated [[gamepad]], or be used unattached. [[Nintendo Switch system software|The system software]] supports [[online game|online gaming]] through internet connectivity, as well as local [[Wireless ad hoc network|wireless ad hoc]] connectivity with other consoles. [[List of Nintendo Switch games|Switch games and software]] are available on physical [[flash storage|flash]]-based [[Nintendo game card|ROM cartridges]] and [[digital distribution of video games|digital distribution]] via [[Nintendo eShop]]; the system has no [[Regional lockout|region lockout]]. Two hardware revisions were released: the handheld-only Switch Lite, released on September 20, 2019; and a higher-end version featuring an [[OLED]] screen, released on October 8, 2021.

The Switch was unveiled on October 20, 2016; the concept came about following Nintendo's financial losses from poor Wii U sales and market competition from [[mobile game]]s. Nintendo's then-president [[Satoru Iwata]] pushed the company towards mobile gaming and novel hardware. The Switch's design was aimed at a wide demographic of players through multiple modes of use. Nintendo preemptively sought the support of many [[Video game developer#Third-party developers|third-party developers and publishers]], as well as [[independent video game|independent]] studios, to help build the game library alongside its first-party games. Standard electronic components, such as a chipset based on [[Nvidia]]'s [[Tegra]] line, were chosen to make game development easier for programmers and more compatible with existing [[game engine]]s.

The Switch received positive reviews, with praise for its innovative concept, intuitive design, and software library, but criticism for certain hardware and controller issues. It became a major commercial success; with over 155&nbsp;million units shipped worldwide {{as of|2025|December|lc=y}}, it is the [[List of best-selling game consoles|second-best-selling console]], behind the [[PlayStation 2]], and the best-selling [[Nintendo console]]. The [[Nintendo Switch 2]], which is [[backward compatible]] with most Switch games, was released on June 5, 2025.

== History ==

=== Background ===
While Nintendo enjoyed record revenues, net sales, and profits in 2009 as a result of the recent releases of the [[Nintendo DS]] and [[Wii]] (in 2004 and 2006 respectively),<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/business/nintendo-defies-recession-with-record-profits-20090507-awdo.html|title=Nintendo defies recession with record profits|date=May 7, 2009|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en|access-date=September 9, 2018|archive-date=September 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909185240/https://www.smh.com.au/business/nintendo-defies-recession-with-record-profits-20090507-awdo.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/21/official-nintendo-ds-launch-details |title=Official Nintendo DS Launch Details |last=Harris |first=Craig |date=September 20, 2004 |website=IGN |language=en-US |access-date=September 9, 2018 |archive-date=September 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909185703/http://www.ign.com/articles/2004/09/21/official-nintendo-ds-launch-details |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="2009 Annual Financial">{{Cite report|publisher=Nintendo|year=2009|access-date=September 3, 2015|title=2009 Annual Financial Report: Financial Section|url=https://www.nintendo.co.jp/ir/pdf/2009/annual0903e.pdf|page=17|archive-date=March 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307051131/https://www.nintendo.co.jp/ir/pdf/2009/annual0903e.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> its revenues soon declined.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://business.time.com/2014/01/17/nintendo-chief-we-failed/|title=Nintendo Chief: 'We Failed'|last=Nicks|first=Denver|date=January 17, 2014|magazine=Time|access-date=March 1, 2019|language=en|issn=0040-781X|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214192209/http://business.time.com/2014/01/17/nintendo-chief-we-failed/|archive-date=December 14, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://time.com/3850264/nintendo-sales-wii-u-3ds-universal-studios/|title=Why Nintendo is Suddenly Profitable Again|last=Luckerson|first=Victor|date=May 7, 2015|magazine=Time|language=en|access-date=March 1, 2019|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304201209/http://time.com/3850264/nintendo-sales-wii-u-3ds-universal-studios/|url-status=live}}</ref> The company posted its first loss as a video game company in 2012 prior to the [[Wii U]]'s introduction that year; Nintendo had similar losses in the following years, due to the console's poor reception.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/25/technology/nintendos-wii-u-takes-aim-at-a-changed-video-game-world.html|title=Nintendo's Wii U Takes Aim at a Changed Video Game
